# Methods {#sec-methods}

## Study Objective

This supplementary analysis evaluates whether a single globally calibrated S2BIOPHYS hybrid PROSAIL inversion model provides comparable performance to vegetation-specific calibrations.

## Data Inputs

Input datasets should be placed in [data/raw](data/raw). Processed artifacts generated by scripts are written to [data/processed](data/processed).

## Model Configurations

We compare:

1. Global model (single calibration).
2. Vegetation-specific models (group-specific calibrations).
3. Optional land-cover-specific models when groups are available.

Validation groups are defined in [config/validation_groups.yml](config/validation_groups.yml).

## Reproducible Workflow

The full workflow is:

1. Build validation groups with [scripts/01_prepare_validation_groups.py](scripts/01_prepare_validation_groups.py).
2. Generate cross-validation splits with [scripts/02_create_cv_splits.py](scripts/02_create_cv_splits.py).
3. Train models with [scripts/03_train_models.py](scripts/03_train_models.py).
4. Evaluate models with [scripts/04_evaluate_models.py](scripts/04_evaluate_models.py).
5. Generate figures and tables with [scripts/05_make_figures_tables.py](scripts/05_make_figures_tables.py).

## Overall model comparison

```{r}
#| label: tbl-global-vs-vegetation
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of the full S2BIOPHYS model, a reduced-budget global model, and vegetation-specific reduced-budget models across validation domains. Performance is reported as RMSE for both ensemble-mean predictions and stacked out-of-sample (SOS) predictions."

library(gt)
library(tibble)

tbl <- tribble(
  ~Validation_domain, ~Full_Ens, ~Full_SOS,
  ~Global_Ens, ~Global_SOS,
  ~Veg_Ens, ~Veg_SOS,

  "Cold-climate evergreen forests", NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "Open tundra vegetation",          NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "Arid shrublands",                 NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "Temperate croplands",             NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "Temperate deciduous & mixed forests", NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "Temperate evergreen forests",     NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "Temperate grasslands",            NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "Temperate non-forest vegetation", NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "Tropical evergreen forests",      NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA
)

tbl |>
  gt(rowname_col = "Validation_domain") |>

  tab_spanner(
    label = md("**S2BIOPHYS full**"),
    columns = c(Full_Ens, Full_SOS)
  ) |>

  tab_spanner(
    label = md("**Global reduced-budget**"),
    columns = c(Global_Ens, Global_SOS)
  ) |>

  tab_spanner(
    label = md("**Vegetation-specific reduced-budget**"),
    columns = c(Veg_Ens, Veg_SOS)
  ) |>

  cols_label(
    Full_Ens   = "Ensemble",
    Full_SOS   = "SOS",
    Global_Ens = "Ensemble",
    Global_SOS = "SOS",
    Veg_Ens    = "Ensemble",
    Veg_SOS    = "SOS"
  ) |>

  fmt_number(
    columns = where(is.numeric),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>

  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = -Validation_domain
  ) |>

  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(10),
    heading.border.bottom.style = "solid",
    table.border.top.width = px(1),
    table.border.bottom.width = px(1),
    data_row.padding = px(3)
  )
```


# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The manuscript-level interpretation should focus on:

1. Whether vegetation-specific calibration improves performance enough to justify complexity.
2. Transferability across vegetation groups and sensitivity to grouping errors.
3. Practical implications for global operational deployment.

# Reproducibility Notes {#sec-reproducibility}

- Keep all supplementary analysis artifacts inside this folder.
- Record package versions and execution date in outputs.
- Prefer deterministic behavior by fixing random seeds in scripts.
